title: Changelog
intro: What have we been up to recently? Find out exactly whats changed in in each version below starting from the most recent changes.

changes.text: Everybody is now shown as their initials on a colour of their own rather than a profile picture. It is the same colour that already marks that person's cursor and selection on the board, so who you are looking at reads the same on the dashboard, on your tutors or students page and in a lesson.

Profile pictures are no longer shown anywhere in the app, and are no longer fetched to draw one. Nothing about how you look is sent between the people in a lesson - your initials and your colour are worked out from your account on each screen that needs them.

There are now forty-eight identity colours rather than ten, so two people in the same lesson are far less likely to be handed the same one. Everyone clears the same legibility floor against the board, and your colour does not change once you have it.

The chalk gradient has been replaced by a single blue accent. It marks the sign-in card, the progress bar as you create a workspace, your plan tag, and the ring around a button you have just been sent to - the places that are the product speaking, rather than anything about a lesson.

The pen now offers eight colours rather than five - chalk, amber, coral, magenta, violet, cyan, green and black. Each is pushed as far as a screen will carry it, so an ink is always brighter than any colour a person can be given and a stroke is never mistaken for somebody's cursor.

Black has been added to the pen. Pasted pages are given a black background, so a black stroke covers what is underneath it rather than drawing on top of it - use it to blank out a worked answer on a past paper before going through it with a student.
The highlighter now offers five colours rather than four - butter, peach, rose, lilac and mint - each lifted to a softer shade so it sits over a stroke without burying it.

The coming up next card is now raised only while the lesson can actually be opened. A tutor sees it lift as soon as the workspace is ready, a student once their tutor has opened it; the rest of the time it sits flat alongside the cards beside it rather than inviting a click that would be turned down.

The length and countdown tags at the bottom of the coming up next card now sit in line with the lesson time, title and description above them rather than under the initials, so everything the card tells you reads down a single edge.

Your plan tag now appears on the plan card at the top of the dashboard only, rather than there and beside the Chalkie Chalkie name in the sidebar. The tier is named once, on the card that already reports what it allows.

The headings inside the create and edit workspace window - title, description, start time, collaborators, friends and feedback, along with the time label on the date picker - are now written as ordinary words rather than in full capitals, so they read as quiet labels for what sits beneath them.

The collaborators heading in that window now reads Collaborators · 2/5, with the count set off by a dot and dimmed behind the word, in the same shape as the participants list inside a lesson, rather than the number being run on to the end of the heading.

The calendar in that window now stops at ninety days ahead. The months past it can no longer be paged to and the days in them can no longer be picked, so a lesson can no longer be dated that far out and then turned down with an unhelpful please try again once you save it.

The warm glow behind the picture on the home page has gone. It was the largest thing the page loaded and it arrived before anything else, so the home page now opens noticeably faster on a slow connection.

The large heading at the top of the dashboard and of your students or tutors page has been replaced by a small trail reading Chalkie Chalkie / Dashboard, or Chalkie Chalkie / Dashboard / Students. It says where you are without taking the top of the page to do it, and every step before the one you are on can be clicked to go back.

The line of description that sat under each of those headings has gone with them. The sidebar and the tabs along the bottom of a phone already mark which page you are on, so the page no longer repeats it back to you in the largest text on screen.

entries.overview: The following changes introduce the framework for tutor plans. While updating your plan is still not possible through the app (coming soon), the following changes lay the groundwork to setup subscriptions for different levels of tutor plans.

changes.text: Accounts now carry a plan, which sets how many people can be in a workspace, how many workspaces you can create in a month, and how many students you can be linked to at once. There is nothing to buy yet - this is the groundwork for it.

The team step of the create and edit workspace window now shows how many people your plan allows against how many you have added. Once you reach it the remaining students are greyed out with a note, rather than letting you pick people the workspace cannot take.

How long before a lesson a workspace opens, and how long it is kept afterwards before being removed, now follow your plan rather than being the same hour and fortnight for every account. A workspace keeps whichever window it was given when it was created.

A workspace now turns people away once it already holds as many as the plan allows, and tells them why, rather than letting a board quietly fill past its limit. The host always keeps a place, so you can never be shut out of your own lesson.

Reaching one of these limits now says which one. Running out of workspaces for the month names the date your allowance resets, and adding too many people names the number your plan allows, in place of the please try again that every failure used to show.
Being turned away for making too many requests in a row now says how long to wait, instead of inviting you to try again straight away.
A tutor can now view their plan teir in the sidebar by the Chalkie Chalkie name.

A workspace's start time no longer freezes the moment its opening window arrives. It stays editable until you open the workspace, or until the start time itself passes. Plans with a longer opening window do not lose editing time because of it.
Opening a workspace now asks the tutor first, so you know the start time is about to be locked before it happens.
Students now wait until their tutor opens the workspace rather than entering an empty board early, and are told that is what they are waiting for.
Workspace statuses now read Ready in 3 days, then Ready to open, then Open. Nothing opens on a schedule any more, so the old Opens in 3 days was no longer true.

Changing your plan applies to everything on your account rather than only to what you make next. How long before a lesson a workspace opens, and how long it is kept afterwards, are brought into line with your new plan across every workspace you have already scheduled. Moving up lengthens them, moving down shortens them.

Nothing is removed the moment a plan ends or moves down. Anything that would otherwise be past its keeping time is held for thirty days first, so there is room to move back up or save what you need. A workspace already close to its own removal date keeps that date rather than being handed longer than it had.

A workspace can no longer be opened once the tutor's plan has ended. Students are told that is the reason rather than being turned away without one, and the lesson says so on the dashboard before you try to join it.

A lesson already under way is never cut short by a plan ending partway through it. Once the tutor has opened the workspace it stays open until the lesson is over, so nobody is dropped mid-lesson and left unable to get back in.

A failed payment no longer stops everything on the spot. Your plan keeps working normally while the payment is retried, and access only ends once it has been given up on or the plan cancelled - so one expired card cannot cancel a week of lessons.

Your monthly workspace allowance runs with your billing period rather than the calendar month, so it refills on the day your plan renews. Starting a plan partway through a month used to give you the rest of that month and then a whole fresh allowance a few days later.

Linked students beyond what your plan allows are made inactive rather than removed. They stay on your list marked as inactive, can be swapped for one another from the row menu, and come back by themselves if you move up a plan - so changing plan never breaks a link you would have to rebuild by trading codes again.

A workspace holding more people than your plan allows is now marked on your dashboard, along with how many to remove. Before this it simply turned the extra people away on the day, and which of them got in came down to who opened it first.
Workspaces can now be scheduled no more than ninety days ahead. A start time further out than that is refused when you save it.

Tutors now have a plan card at the top of the dashboard showing how many workspaces they have made this billing period and how many students they have linked, each against what the plan allows, with the date the workspace allowance refills. Underneath it names how many people a lesson can hold and how long boards are kept. Reaching either limit is marked on the card rather than only being found out when something is refused.

The plan card takes the place the getting started checklist had, and only once the checklist has gone - so the two are never shown together. There is nothing to report before a first lesson has run, and nothing left to teach after it.

A getting started checklist now walks you through the three steps before your first lesson. It takes over the page while there is nothing on it yet, and reads differently for a tutor and a student since the two start from different places.

The checklist steps back to a card once a page has something of its own to show - beside the coming up next card on the dashboard, above the table on your tutors or students page - so each page makes room for its own content as soon as it has any. It disappears altogether once your first lesson has started.

Students who have not linked a tutor yet can now request a tutor account from the checklist. The form asks what you teach, roughly how many students you have and where you tutor now; your name, email and account are attached automatically.
The coming up next card now keeps its tags at the foot of the card and holds a minimum height, so it ends level with the checklist beside it rather than the pair finishing at different points.

The dashboard and your tutors or students page now wait for everything they have asked for before drawing, rather than filling in as each answer arrives. A step you had already completed could briefly show as outstanding while the rest of the page loaded.
The dashboard sidebar can now be collapsed to a strip of icons using the Collapse button at the foot of it. Hovering an icon names it while collapsed.
Whether the sidebar was left collapsed or expanded is now remembered between visits, and applied before the page is drawn so nothing shifts as it loads.

The dashboard now uses its full layout on tablets, with the sidebar, filters and workspace tables as they appear on a desktop, rather than the narrower phone version it showed before. Phone screens keep the layout they had.

The sidebar now starts collapsed to its icons on a tablet and expanded on wider screens, so a narrower window keeps more of its width for the workspace tables. Setting it with the Collapse button still overrides this at every screen size.

The next card now sizes itself against the room the sidebar leaves rather than always taking the same share of it. On a tablet it spans the full width, and on a smaller laptop it does the same while the sidebar is expanded, narrowing to half the row once the sidebar is collapsed. Wider screens are unchanged.
Workspaces can now be joined from a tablet, through the next card or a workspace's menu, rather than only from a desktop. Phones still cannot open a board.

The tabs, search and column headings above a workspace table now stay pinned to the top of the page as you scroll, so you can see which column you are reading and switch tab without scrolling back up. Only the page title and the next card scroll away.

Row height can now be set to compact, default or comfortable from the new button beside Clear filters, so you can fit more workspaces on screen or give each one more room. The setting is remembered between visits and applies to your connections as well.

The workspace and connections tables now give every column a minimum width and scroll sideways when there is not enough room for all of them, rather than squeezing each column into a fixed share of the width. Columns still share out any spare space on a wide screen.

A workspace's header, or a person's name on the connections page, now stays pinned to the left of its row while the table is scrolled sideways, and the row's menu stays pinned to the right, so a row can always be identified and acted on.

The [cookie policy](/cookie-policy) now covers the two cookies that remember the sidebar setting and the row height. Neither holds anything that identifies you, and each is only stored once you have used the control that sets it.
The navigation bar now uses a frosted background rather than fading into the page behind it, so it stays legible over whatever it covers, and sits closer to the edges on narrow screens.
Workspace creation and modification dialog would reset intermittently, this bug has been fixed.
Clear filters button styling updated for consistency between itself and other button states.
Students would see their tutor icon in the next card and their own icon in the workspace list, this bug has been fixed.
Increased workspace grace period when moving from upcoming to previous tabs from 5 minutes to 10 minutes.
Workspaces now open an hour before the lesson begins rather than from the moment they are created, so a board can only be joined around the session it was made for.

A workspace's start time is fixed once it has opened. Everything else stays editable, so feedback can still be written after the lesson; if a session is not going ahead, delete the workspace instead of moving it.
Workspaces are now removed 14 days after their start time rather than after 14 days without activity, so how long a board and its feedback are kept, is known the moment it is scheduled.

A status against every workspace showing where it is in that cycle - when it opens, that it is ready to join, or how long is left before it is deleted - counting down live without needing a page refresh.

Joining is now disabled, rather than failing on arrival, while a workspace is closed, and says why. A board opened directly outside its window explains whether it has not opened yet, has no start time, or has already been removed.

Warnings when scheduling a workspace that will not behave as expected: one with no start time cannot be opened and is deleted the same night, and one booked inside the opening hour opens straight away with its start time locked on save.
Changelog entries are now dated by the day a version went live rather than the day its code was written, so the dates line up with when the changes actually reached the app.
The loader for the search sessions input, within the dashboard, has been updated to match the styling of the loaded input.
The version you are running is now shown in the footer of the home page, beside the copyright, and is written with a v prefix everywhere it appears.

Erasing no longer makes a board re-count everything it has ever held each time something is rubbed out. This was by far the largest source of database work during a lesson, and a busy board now costs a small fraction of what it did.
The eraser sends its changes a little less often while it is being dragged. Rubbing out feels the same, but a long sweep across a full board is a fraction of the work it was.

A board now accepts at most three connections at once from the same person, so one account cannot hold a room open across a dozen tabs. A fourth tab waits instead of joining, and connects as soon as one of the others is closed.

Rejoining the same board over and over is now limited, since every join reloads the whole drawing. Ordinary use is unaffected and a few reloads in a row are fine, but a run of rapid reconnections is held back until it settles.
Users now get evicted from the workspace if they are removed by a tutor instead of their access persisting until their next page reload.
The nightly clean-up of inactive workspaces now works in batches within a time limit, so a large backlog is cleared over several nights rather than timing out.
Corrected inconsistencies between styling of the coming up next card's empty and loading states.
Deleting a workspace now fully releases its realtime storage. Previously every deleted board left an empty room behind that was never reclaimed.
Deleting a workspace while its board was still open could leave that room's storage behind. It is now cleared either way.

changes: Chalkie Chalkie's minimal-production release. This includes all basic features that the app will continue to develop and sets up the infrastructre to build upon.

changes.text: Migrated image storage from Supabase to Cloudflare R2.
Migrated realtime infrastructure from Liveblocks to Cloudflare workers & durable objects.
